gates.name: AI gateway preview qualification
gates.description: An entitled account in the staged rollout calls its provider through the relay with redaction, settlement, cost and a hard daily cap; every forwarded call settles its usage, Postgres or provider failures fail closed or cost nothing, and closing the release gate is the rollback (ADR-998).

gates.name: Declared contract and effective policy preview
gates.description: A deployment can compare declared routes with observed routes and matching edge policy without mutating production.

gates.name: Consumer billing accuracy
gates.description: Consumer usage is priced per minute with the effective rate card, late usage only adds adjustment revisions, and billed usage is checkable against request telemetry before invoicing.

gates.name: Application inbox and outbox reliability
gates.description: Accepted application messages are persisted through the existing invocation and signed webhook delivery ledgers.

gates.name: Capability acceptance: account
gates.description: Each released account capability passes its catalogued acceptance test before it is offered to an account (ADR-20261023115741).

gates.name: Capability acceptance: async
gates.description: Each released async capability passes its catalogued acceptance test before it is offered to an account (ADR-20261023115741).

gates.name: Capability acceptance: billing
gates.description: Each released billing capability passes its catalogued acceptance test before it is offered to an account (ADR-20261023115741).

gates.name: Capability acceptance: data
gates.description: Each released data capability passes its catalogued acceptance test before it is offered to an account (ADR-20261023115741).

gates.name: Capability acceptance: delivery
gates.description: Each released delivery capability passes its catalogued acceptance test before it is offered to an account (ADR-20261023115741).

gates.name: Capability acceptance: developer
gates.description: Each released developer capability passes its catalogued acceptance test before it is offered to an account (ADR-20261023115741).

gates.name: Capability acceptance: edge
gates.description: Each released edge capability passes its catalogued acceptance test before it is offered to an account (ADR-20261023115741).

gates.name: Capability acceptance: observability
gates.description: Each released observability capability passes its catalogued acceptance test before it is offered to an account (ADR-20261023115741).

gates.name: Capability acceptance: runtime
gates.description: Each released runtime capability passes its catalogued acceptance test before it is offered to an account (ADR-20261023115741).

gates.name: Application companion readiness
gates.description: A bounded companion boots with the application, remains isolated by its own resource controls, and preserves the shared instance lifecycle contract.

gates.name: Normal OCI container compatibility
gates.description: A stateless Linux/amd64 OCI image can preserve its process contract and use the full-rootfs path when it is not built from a Gregale base.

gates.name: Declarative response-cache readiness
gates.description: A route-level response cache serves an eligible stale response while a single background refresh restores freshness, with an operator recovery path for purge and distributed-cache failures.

gates.name: Delayed execution reliability
gates.description: A delayed invocation is durably scheduled for a bounded future time, reaches the app through the normal gateway bridge, and can be cancelled before dispatch without reaching the workload.

gates.name: Disposable isolated execution
gates.description: Untrusted source is admitted only through authenticated, bounded, networkless disposable execution and its payload is not returned in customer reads.

gates.name: Durable inbound webhook reliability
gates.description: A provider-signed webhook is durably accepted before acknowledgement, deduplicated across provider retries, and queued for the normal wake and delivery lifecycle.

gates.name: AI crawler controls release qualification
gates.description: AI crawler conditions match the User-Agent claim and purpose and, for operators that publish ranges, verify it; the published ranges refresh and expire; the recipe blocks or challenges by purpose; the summary counts each crawler; and the edge_ai_crawlers platform flag makes the conditions absent and unconfigurable for accounts it leaves out (ADR-20261022083601, ADR-20261024082000).

gates.name: Attack mode release qualification
gates.description: Attack mode switches on for a bounded time, extends and ends on its own, stays outside quotas and rollbacks, refuses PATCH, and is switched on only while both edge_attack_mode and edge_challenge include the account; withdrawing edge_attack_mode leaves an active attack mode inert (ADR-20261021220456, ADR-20261024082000).

gates.name: Browser challenge (generally available)
gates.description: A browser navigation on a challenged route solves the page and passes on its pass while a script is refused with 403 challenge_required, verified credentials and crawlers pass, the browser's solver agrees with the gateway, raised difficulty is capped and falls back, and the edge_challenge platform flag makes rules inert for accounts it leaves out (ADR-831 amendments 7-8, ADR-20261023113721, ADR-20261024082000).

gates.name: Edge penalty box release qualification
gates.description: A rule with a penalty boxes a client after its threshold of policy refusals and refuses it on every path with 403 penalty_box and Retry-After, lets it go when the rule loses its penalty, stays within its per-app and per-gateway caps, and the edge_penalty_box platform flag stops boxing for accounts it leaves out (ADR-20261022105846, ADR-20261023113721, ADR-20261024082000).

gates.name: WAF warn and block (generally available)
gates.description: On the reference compute node the in-path check stays within 2 ms at p95 and skips at most 0.1% of checks at 100-500 req/s, detects the CRS regression corpus with no benign request flagged beyond the documented ones, fails open, and the edge_waf_blocking platform flag inspects warn and block rules as observe for accounts it leaves out (ADR-831 amendments 4-12, ADR-20261023113721, ADR-20261024082000).

gates.name: Time to first healthy API
gates.description: A clean-account deployment reaches a verified public response within the onboarding budget.

gates.name: Zero-config framework compatibility
gates.description: The maintained API fixture catalog continues to infer a runnable profile for supported frameworks and source shapes.

gates.name: Grouped failure triage and recovery
gates.description: Accepted failures preserve grouping and release history, enforce scoped ownership and resolution, and recover committed notifications without counting exact retries twice.

gates.name: Stateless MCP hosting qualification
gates.description: The stateless MCP starter passes discovery, explicit calls, streaming, Origin policy and failure recovery through the existing application lifecycle. Native receipts record park and restored qualification; untouched lockfile deployment and external-provider interoperability remain release qualification requirements.

gates.name: Pull-request preview readiness
gates.description: A preview deployment gets an isolated, reviewable URL inside the GitHub event budget.

gates.name: Production forks and crash snapshots
gates.description: A crash capture, manual capture or live capture opens only as a quarantined fork that is never routed, cannot open outbound flows, runs commands only inside the fork, keeps captures encrypted at rest, and is destroyed at its TTL with no leaked resources (ADR-732, ADR-733).

gates.name: Request diagnosis
gates.description: A request timeline preserves route, latency, wake, and error evidence without requiring payload capture.

gates.name: Bound resource readiness
gates.description: A customer-facing resource binding has qualification evidence before it is promoted beyond internal use.

gates.name: Rollback recovery
gates.description: A bad deployment can be rolled back without rebuilding and traffic returns healthy inside the recovery budget. Recovery includes shifting traffic between revisions and holding a canary ladder when health signals degrade, so a bad release can be contained before it reaches every request.

gates.name: Route change safety
gates.description: Route changes are reviewed before release: source impact maps a diff to affected endpoints, saved route requirements check authentication, throttle and budget policy, lifecycle review keeps a route that still has customer traffic or a saved requirement from being retired without evidence, and the route advisor proposes cache, async and throttle rules from observed traffic that are created disabled for review.

gates.name: Route release protection
gates.description: A release that breaks a critical route is caught per route rather than in aggregate: canary route health is seeded by customer reach and judges sparse routes over pooled or synthetic evidence, and production route budgets can request one checked rollback to the last healthy deployment when an error budget is violated within 30 minutes of release.

gates.name: Internal service reachability and isolation
gates.description: A same-account service is reachable by name, a parked one is woken by the call rather than refused, its configured wire protocol survives to the guest, and a private app stays off the public edge while cross-account callers are denied.

gates.name: SLO budgets and synthetic checks
gates.description: Customer SLO budgets are computed from the recorded hourly attainment, and synthetic checks record every run's outcome, status and latency.

gates.name: Snapshot wake recovery
gates.description: A parked API wakes through the snapshot path and serves a public request within the platform restore budget.

gates.name: Worker pool readiness
gates.description: A worker deployment validates its long-lived execution mode and restart defaults before it is admitted.

gates.name: Asynchronous work reliability
gates.description: Background workflows preserve plan policy and complete their lifecycle without leaking platform state.
